title: Lattice Theta Functions with Half-Integral Characteristics
description:
Exact proofs, certificates, and reproducible computations for identical vanishing of lattice theta functions with half-integral characteristics.

The symmetry converse holds in ranks one through three and fails in rank four. The rank-four results of versions 1.1.0 to 1.3.0: an identically vanishing even characteristic of a lattice of determinant 1729 whose two coset lattices are the Conway–Sloane isospectral pair L-(1,7,13,19), L+(1,7,13,19), which are not isometric (eight such configurations are certified), and the smallest such zero, an odd lattice of determinant 280 with automorphism group {I, −I}; the minimum determinant of a rank-four counterexample to the symmetry converse is 280, proved by complete isometry-class lists through determinant 279 (the determinant-24 census and seven class lists, every vanishing even characteristic witnessed by an automorphism, each list independently replayed), with exactly one failing class at determinant 280; an even counterexample of determinant 1156 with automorphism group {I, −I}, the same Eisenstein-integer construction as the original determinant-23,716 example and the minimum of that family; and the rank-four parity property, which fails for indecomposable odd lattices with determinant not divisible by four first at determinant 49 and for even indecomposable lattices of odd determinant first at determinant 121 (a Gaussian-integer structure), with complete class lists and structural theorems. Version 1.3.0 adds, for even indecomposable lattices of odd determinant, a classification of symmetry zeros (each comes from an automorphism whose square is −I, so lattices of determinant 5 mod 8 have none), a reduction showing that any zero of determinant 5 mod 8 would have to be a pair of isospectral, non-isometric coset lattices, and complete class lists of all even lattices of odd determinant through 501 (1,890 classes) whose only zeros are the predicted ones, at determinants 121 and 361. Version 1.4.0 proves the minus-type parity conjecture at every determinant: an even, orthogonally indecomposable rank-four lattice of determinant 5 mod 8 has no identically vanishing nontrivial even characteristic, and in every even rank-four lattice of odd determinant such a zero is a symmetry zero. The proof is computer-assisted (Theorem S): an exact classification over the faces of Voronoi’s three primitive cones of quaternary forms, 502,740 cases each with an exact certificate, audited and independently replayed. Two further deductions from an independent assessment are included: the ordinary theta series does not determine the parity property in rank four, and a determinant-3844 isospectral non-isometric pair is proved at every level by weight-two Sturm bounds.

The release also includes the low-rank parity classification, the classification of irreducible crystallographic root lattices in the stated normalization, exact determinant-at-most-24 censuses through rank four, and a checked literature note on the isospectrality sources. No literature-priority claim is made.

Reproduction uses Python 3.11 or later and the Python standard library only. The included reviews are AI-assisted local mathematical reviews with independent computational replication. They are not a claim of journal publication or formal peer review.
